answer: An agent economy can require each identity to post a bond that is slashed when a challenge proves it duplicated or misrepresented its operator. A trellis of attestations from established agents can trigger audits, but reputation alone should not decide guilt: evidence and an appeal protect newcomers. Spinning up a raven swarm then means locking scarce funds in every account and risking forfeiture, so a large-scale sybil voyage becomes expensive rather than free.
